scams.name: Old San Juan '$500 Parking Ticket' & Street-Parking Scam
scams.description:
Old San Juan has complex parking rules. Metered street spaces require quarters or the ParkMobile app, many blocks are residential-only with two-hour tourist restrictions, and some "parking attendants" in reflective vests are unauthorized individuals demanding a $10–$20 "parking fee" for free or metered spaces — and then the car gets a legitimate ticket anyway. Travelers report tickets totaling $500 from a combination of an expired meter, a residential-zone violation, and a towing fee.

The scam has several variants: an unauthorized "parking attendant" demanding cash for a free street space; "private parking lot" signs pointing to unmarked residential driveways that tow within one hour; a meter expired for just 10 minutes leading to a $50–$100 ticket plus a same-day tow at $300 or more; and fake online parking-ticket "payment portal" websites after you find a ticket on your windshield.

For older travelers visiting Old San Juan, the clean playbook is straightforward. Park only at the official Paseo Covadonga lot ($8/day) or the Doña Fela lot ($5/day), and avoid street parking entirely. If a "parking attendant" in a reflective vest demands cash for a street space, refuse and find official parking. Download ParkMobile for any metered spaces, and read all signs carefully, since residential-only zones tow within one hour. If you do get a ticket, pay only via sanjuan.pr.gov or in person at the Municipal Court — never through websites linked from the ticket, which are fake. Better still, take an Uber or taxi into Old San Juan from your hotel ($8–$15) and skip parking altogether.
scams.avoidance: Park only at the Paseo Covadonga ($8/day) or Doña Fela ($5/day) official lots. Refuse unauthorized "parking attendants" demanding cash. Download ParkMobile for metered spaces. Pay tickets only via sanjuan.pr.gov or in person at the Municipal Court. Better yet, take an Uber or taxi into Old San Juan ($8–$15) and skip parking.
scams.location: Old San Juan street parking, Calle San Sebastián / Calle del Cristo parking, Plaza Colón area, Paseo Covadonga paid lots
scams.tldr: Old San Juan parking is a minefield of unauthorized "attendants" charging for free spaces, residential-only towing zones, and fake online ticket-payment sites — one combination of violations can total $500.

scams.name: San Juan (SJU) Airport Taxi & Rideshare Overcharge
scams.description:
SJU is 7 miles from Old San Juan and 12 miles from the Condado and Isla Verde resorts. Puerto Rico has regulated airport taxi flat rates ("tarifa autorizada"): Old San Juan $21, Condado $19, Isla Verde $14–$17, and Miramar $21 per trip — not per person, and good for up to five passengers. These rates are posted at the airport taxi stand, so a driver quoting higher is scamming you. Uber is legal at SJU and runs $12–$20 to most destinations, with pickup at Zone E (the ground-transportation curb).

The scam has several variants: a driver at baggage claim offering a "flat $45" to Old San Juan when the regulated rate is $21; a driver insisting Uber is "not allowed" at SJU (it is); a "luggage fee" or "night rate" tacked on beyond the flat rate (the flat rate is flat, with no add-ons); and a driver demanding a cash tip beyond the flat rate.

For older travelers arriving at SJU, the clean playbook is simple. Go to the official Autoridad de Transporte Público (ATP) tourist taxi stand — look for the white kiosk with posted flat rates. Pay the posted flat rate exactly: Old San Juan $21, Condado $19, Isla Verde $14–$17, Miramar $21, plus a standard $1–$3 luggage tip. Uber at the Zone E rideshare pickup is a legal alternative and often cheaper ($12–$20 to most destinations). Refuse any driver quoting higher than the posted flat rate, since the next driver in the queue will honor the posted rates. Print or screenshot the flat-rate chart from prtc.pr.gov before you arrive. And do not tip beyond the flat rate if a driver adds a "luggage fee" or "night rate" — instead, report it to ATP at 787-756-1919.
scams.avoidance: Use the official ATP tourist taxi stand with posted flat rates. The flat rates are Old San Juan $21, Condado $19, Isla Verde $14–$17, Miramar $21. Uber at the Zone E rideshare pickup is legal ($12–$20 to most destinations). Refuse drivers quoting above the posted flat rate and take the next queued driver. Print the flat-rate chart from prtc.pr.gov before arrival.
scams.location: Luis Muñoz Marín International Airport (SJU), TransporTaxi stand, rideshare pickup Zone E, Carolina-adjacent pickup
scams.tldr: SJU has posted, regulated taxi flat rates (Old San Juan $21, Condado $19, Isla Verde $14–$17, Miramar $21); any driver quoting higher or claiming Uber is banned is scamming you.

scams.name: Puerto Rico Rental Car 'Sixt' / 'NextCar' Damage & Deposit Scam
scams.description:
Rental-car fraud in Puerto Rico is severe. Sixt Puerto Rico has a documented pattern of $2,000–$5,000 post-return damage claims for scratches that existed at pickup. NextCar, an off-airport budget operator, has a documented pattern of "pre-authorization" deposits of $250–$500 that are held and not returned for 6–12 weeks after the car is returned. "Off-airport discount" operators advertise "SJU rentals at $15/day" on third-party websites that then vanish with the deposit. Some operators rent a "toll transponder" (AutoExpreso) at $15/day when you can buy the transponder for $10 at any Pueblo grocery. And there is "local collision insurance" pressure at $35/day, even though the Puerto Rico insurance-law mandate is already included in most US credit-card rental coverage.

For older travelers renting in Puerto Rico, the clean playbook is clear. Use Enterprise, Hertz, or Alamo at SJU — the most reliable operators per 2025 reviews — and avoid Sixt PR, NextCar, Payless, and all off-airport budget operators. At pickup, record a video walk-around narrating every scratch, tire, wheel, and windshield, and timestamp all photos. Decline "local collision insurance" if your credit card provides rental coverage, since Chase Sapphire, Amex Platinum, and most Visa Signature cards work in Puerto Rico. For the toll transponder, buy AutoExpreso at any Pueblo grocery for $10 rather than renting it from the operator at $15/day. Return the car with the fuel level documented at pickup. Dispute any post-return damage claim with your credit card within 48 hours. And screenshot any pre-authorization deposits, then follow up in 7 days if they are not released.
scams.avoidance: Use Enterprise, Hertz, or Alamo at SJU, and avoid Sixt PR, NextCar, and Payless. Record a video walk-around at pickup narrating every scratch, tire, and wheel. Decline "local collision" coverage if your credit card covers rentals. Buy an AutoExpreso transponder at a Pueblo grocery ($10) rather than from the rental company ($15/day). Dispute post-return claims via your credit card within 48 hours.
scams.location: SJU airport rental facility, San Juan Isla Grande rental offices, Condado / Isla Verde partner rental operators, off-airport 'budget' rental lots
scams.tldr: Puerto Rico rental fraud runs from Sixt's $2,000–$5,000 phantom damage claims to NextCar's unreturned deposits and overpriced toll transponders; stick to major operators and document everything.

scams.name: El Yunque & 'GetYourGuide' Tour Overcharge with Cancellation Risk
scams.description:
Cancellations and refund refusals on the GetYourGuide platform are a known problem for Puerto Rico tours. El Yunque is the only tropical rainforest in the US National Forest system and the most-booked Puerto Rico excursion. Legitimate operators include AdvenTours ($79–$125 group tours), EcoQuest PR ($89–$140), and Island Journeys ($75–$120).

The scam has several variants: third-party "GetYourGuide" or "Viator" operators canceling day-of and then refusing a refund beyond a "credit"; hotel-concierge "El Yunque VIP" packages at $250–$400 for what costs $89 booked direct; "private El Yunque mobility tours" at $500 or more when AdvenTours and EcoQuest offer legitimate accessibility-focused tours at $150–$180; and "El Yunque waterfall and beach combo" day-long packages at $200 or more that include only 90 minutes in the forest.

For older travelers who want to visit El Yunque from San Juan, the clean playbook is simple. Book direct with AdvenTours (adventourspr.com, $89–$125), EcoQuest PR (ecoquestpr.com, $89–$140), or Island Journeys. For mobility concerns, request accessibility-focused tours; AdvenTours and EcoQuest offer shorter-walk routes to Yokahú Tower and La Coca Falls without strenuous hiking. Avoid GetYourGuide third-party listings and use the direct operator websites only. Remember that El Yunque itself is free to enter via the El Portal Visitor Center, with forested trails accessible — you pay only for guided transportation from San Juan ($89–$140). And pay by credit card, not Zelle.
scams.avoidance: Book direct with AdvenTours ($89–$125), EcoQuest PR ($89–$140), or Island Journeys. Request accessibility-focused tours for mobility concerns. Avoid GetYourGuide third-party listings and use direct operator sites. El Yunque itself is free — you pay only for transportation from San Juan. Pay by credit card for chargeback leverage.
scams.location: El Yunque National Forest operator booking sites, hotel-concierge tour desks, Old San Juan tour-kiosk strip, third-party reseller websites
scams.tldr: El Yunque tours are oversold through third-party platforms like GetYourGuide that cancel and refuse refunds, while the forest itself is free; book direct with reputable operators ($89–$140).

scams.name: San Juan Airbnb Off-Platform Booking & 'PR Robbery' Pattern
scams.description:
Airbnb break-ins occur in Puerto Rico, often tied to "hosts" who share guest-arrival codes or leave keys in lockboxes with publicly visible codes. Off-platform short-term-rental fraud also surges during Puerto Rico concert and event tourism, including Bad Bunny concert weekends.

The scam has several variants: "off-platform" listings where a "host" asks for Zelle, Venmo, or a wire transfer at a "15–25% discount" for a listing that is fake; cloned legitimate Airbnb listings copied to Facebook Marketplace, Craigslist, Craigslist-PR, or Instagram; legitimate Airbnb stays where "hosts" pre-share arrival codes and the unit is broken into during the stay; "Bad Bunny concert weekend" last-minute rentals with Zelle-only payment; and "party rental" or "wedding rental" packages at inflated prices through unverified operators.

For older travelers booking accommodation in Puerto Rico, the protective playbook is essential. Book only through the Airbnb, VRBO, or Booking.com platform payment systems — never Zelle, Venmo, Cash App, or wire transfer. For in-unit security, change the lockbox code on arrival if the host uses an electronic keypad, never store valuables in the "host's storage room," and photograph the serial numbers of all valuables at check-in. Consider hotels for higher-crime zones: the Caribe Hilton, La Concha, Fairmont El San Juan, El Convento, or Hotel La Terraza in Condado, Isla Verde, and Old San Juan. For concerts and festivals (Bad Bunny, Calle 13, Festival Casals), book six or more months ahead, since last-minute social-media offers are almost always scams. And report any break-in to the PRPD (787-793-1234) and to Airbnb within 24 hours. This scam pattern recurs across Puerto Rico.
scams.avoidance: Book only through Airbnb, VRBO, or Booking.com platform payment. Never pay via Zelle, Venmo, Cash App, or wire transfer. Consider hotels for security: the Caribe Hilton, La Concha, Fairmont El San Juan, or El Convento. Change the lockbox code on arrival if possible, and photograph valuables at check-in. For concerts and festivals, book six or more months ahead rather than through last-minute social media.
scams.location: Condado / Isla Verde / Miramar / Old San Juan short-term rentals, off-platform 'Airbnb' operators
scams.tldr: Off-platform "Airbnb" listings demanding Zelle or wire payment are fake, and even legitimate stays risk lockbox break-ins; book only through platform payment and secure your valuables on arrival.

scams.name: Condado / Isla Verde Timeshare Presentation Hustle
scams.description:
Condado and Isla Verde host major timeshare-sales operations targeting cruise passengers, resort guests, and older retirees. Promoters in hotel lobbies or cruise-pier areas offer a "free San Juan tour," a "$150 dinner voucher," or a "free catamaran sail" in exchange for a "90-minute presentation." The presentation actually runs three to five hours, with aggressive pushing of $15,000–$60,000 "vacation ownership" or "travel club" purchases.

The scam has several variants: cruise-pier "photo booth" promoters offering a "free Puerto Rico tour" that turns out to be a timeshare pitch; Condado hotel-lobby "concierge" promoters in plainclothes who are actually timeshare sales staff; "Vacation Club" memberships at $10,000–$25,000 with opaque annual fees; and "exit" companies charging $5,000–$15,000 upfront to "cancel an existing timeshare," many of which are themselves scams. The same patterns appear in Charleston, Scottsdale, and Branson.

For older travelers in San Juan, the defensive posture is firm. Never accept "free gift" offers in cruise-pier areas, Condado hotel lobbies, or Isla Verde resorts — the time cost makes it a net loss even with the gift. If you do attend, bring a printed "I will not sign anything today" rule and stick to it. Puerto Rico offers a 7-day right of rescission for timeshare contracts under the Timeshare Real Estate Law; cancel within 7 days by certified mail. For rescission help, contact the Puerto Rico Department of Consumer Affairs (DACO) at 787-722-7555. Avoid "exit" companies charging $5,000 or more upfront and use DACO directly. And report any high-pressure timeshare tactics to DACO and the BBB.
scams.avoidance: Refuse all "free gift" offers from cruise-pier and hotel-lobby promoters. If you attend, bring an "I will not sign anything today" rule and stick to it. Use Puerto Rico's 7-day right of rescission (DACO, 787-722-7555). Avoid "exit" companies charging $5,000 or more and use DACO directly. Report high-pressure tactics to DACO and the BBB.
scams.location: Condado Avenida Ashford timeshare kiosks, Isla Verde resort lobbies, San Juan cruise-pier promoter booths
scams.tldr: In Condado and Isla Verde, "free tour" and dinner-voucher offers lead to three-to-five-hour timeshare pitches pushing $15,000–$60,000 purchases; decline the gift and never sign on the day.
